findings.evidence: Line 297: `have h0 := (hg.continuousAt.tendsto.mul h_pow)...` is the only use of hg; no other invocation of analyticity in either declaration.
findings.fix: Weaken the hypothesis to `hg : ContinuousAt g s` in both the helper and the public engine (proof unchanged: use `hg.tendsto.mul h_pow`). AnalyticAt callers still supply this via `.continuousAt`.
findings.issue: laurent_coeff_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq_analytic (public engine) and its helper coeff_top_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq_analytic (line 262) assume `AnalyticAt ℂ g s`, but analyticity is only ever used via `hg.continuousAt` (line 297). findings.evidence: Line 365: `laurent_coeff_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq_analytic (hh.sub hg) h_diff ...` is the only use of hg/hh.
findings.fix: Weaken to `hg hh : ContinuousAt`, replacing `hh.sub hg` with `ContinuousAt.sub`; the meromorphic wrapper laurent_coeff_eq_meromorphicPolarCoeffAt still passes analytic parts via `.continuousAt`.
findings.issue: laurent_coeff_unique assumes `hg hh : AnalyticAt` for both remainders but uses them only through `hh.sub hg` (line 365) into the zero-lemma; continuity suffices.

summary: The uniqueness engine and its helpers carry AnalyticAt remainder hypotheses that the proofs use only through continuity; the natural level is ContinuousAt, which strictly widens reuse and keeps every current caller valid.
